subject: English
question_text: Read the following text and fill in each gap with a
stimulus: suitable word based on the information of the text.15 = 5 To be a good citizen, you have to prepare yourself to do good work in society. Well, then how can you prepare yourself? First, you need knowledge. Today's society is knowledge based. Without having knowledge of modern science, technologies, including ICT and other necessary subjects, you will have difficult living a good life. The other areas you, as a good citizen, should have knowledge about are : our country, its constitution, geography, people, state, its executive and legislative powers, judicial system, government and its structure and functions, history, cultures, traditions, literature, moral values and religions, socio-economic activities and religions. Second, you need skills to do things. Knowledge is not enough. You must be able to apply your knowledge to do things practically. Finally, knowing and doing things will bring about a change in your behavour towards others. This behavioured change will show your attitudes towards others, that is, it will show how you think and feel about a person or thing. [Unit-1; Lesson-2] For (a) ⎯ a good citizen, one (b) ⎯ knowledge (c) ⎯ today's society is knowledge based. A good citizen must have knowledge about modern science, technologies, country, constitution etc. (d) ⎯ a good citizen must have skills. Knowledge together with skills (e) ⎯ behavioural changes towards others which is called attitudes. Read the passage and answer the questions 4 and 5. The Rohingya people, historically also termed Arakanese Indians, are a stateless Indo-Aryan people from Rakhine State, Myammar. There were an estimated I million Rohingya living in Myanmar before the 2016-17 crisis. The majority are Muslim while a minority are Hindu. Described by the United Nations in 2013 as one of the most persecuted minorities in the world, the Rohingya population are denied citizenship under 1982 laws "effectively deny to the Rohingya the possibility of acquiring a nationality. Despite being able to trace Rohingya history to the 8th century, Burmese law does not recognize the ethnic minority as one of the eight "national races." They are also restricted from freedom of movement, state education of civil jobs. The legal constions faced by the Rohingya in Myanmar have been compared with apartheid.
